claims.text: The proposed feedstock is AlCrFeNiSi powder with controlled particle-size distribution.
The AlCrFeNiSi feedstock composition is similar to material used in prior PBF-LB studies.
In-situ secondary infrared heating with closed-loop control can maintain the entire build chamber and substrate near 600°C.
Heating the build during PBF-LB will reduce thermal gradients.
Reducing rapid-cooling-induced thermal gradients will reduce residual thermal stresses.
A maintained moderate-temperature environment near 600°C will promote controlled nonequilibrium short-range-order evolution in AlCrFeNiSi.
A maintained temperature near 600°C will promote grain recrystallization in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Controlled short-range order and grain recrystallization will produce a refined and homogenized microstructure.
Closed-loop temperature monitoring will ensure uniform temperature distribution throughout the build.
Uniform closed-loop temperature control will prevent localized overheating, unwanted phase transformations, and oxidation.
The heated process will produce significantly lower residual stresses than conventional high-thermal-load PBF-LB.
The refined microstructure will improve the strength-ductility balance relative to conventional high-thermal-load PBF-LB.
The intervention will reduce or eliminate the need for post-build heat treatment.
Conventional high-thermal-load PBF-LB without in-situ heating produces high residual thermal stresses.
Conventional high-thermal-load PBF-LB without in-situ heating produces degraded mechanical properties.
The proposed processing window is approximately 600°C and 50-70 J/mm³.
The proposed geometry is a miniature component approximately 2 mm in diameter and 5 mm high.
Mechanical performance will be assessed using room-temperature tensile and compression tests.
The effects of the intervention on larger components and other additive-manufacturing regimes are undetermined.
